name: Lightning Attention-2: A Free Lunch for Handling Unlimited Sequence Lengths in Large Language Models
problem: Linear attention is theoretically linear-time, but the CUMULATIVE SUMMATION needed to compute it destroys the theoretical advantage in the causal (autoregressive) setting - so in practice linear attention is not faster than attention.
mechanism: Tiling. Split the causal linear-attention computation into intra-block and inter-block parts: compute the intra-block portion with CONVENTIONAL attention machinery (dense, small, well-shaped) and the inter-block portion with linear-attention kernel tricks. A tiling technique is applied in BOTH forward and backward so the IO pattern suits the GPU. Implemented in Triton, explicitly IO-aware.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract), qualitative-plus-conditional: Lightning Attention-2 'retains consistent training and inference speed REGARDLESS of input sequence length' and is 'significantly faster than other attention mechanisms'. No multiple with a named baseline appears in the abstract. The load-bearing quantitative property is the CONSTANT-INDEPENDENCE from sequence length, which is a different kind of claim from a speedup.
notes: arXiv ID 2401.04658 verified via abs-page citation_title/citation_date on 2026-10-03; title matches. venue=arxiv-preprint: comment says only 'Technical Report', and OpenReview search for this title returns only LATER papers (a NeurIPS 2024 ICML.workshop submission and 'Can Mamba Always Enjoy the Free Lunch?', ICLR 2025) - no venue for this paper itself. adoption=abandoned - the sharpest call in this batch and the basis is checked, not assumed: the official repo OpenNLPLab/lightning-attention was last pushed 2025-02-23 (over a year before this verification date) with 344 stars; its sibling repo OpenNLPLab/TransnormerLLM was last pushed 2024-01-23; and NEITHER Lightning Attention nor TransNormer appears in vLLM's registry, vLLM's 30-file v1 attention backend list, SGLang's 248-file models directory, SGLang's attention backend list, or transformers cache_utils.py. The technique survives only indirectly - TransNormerLLM's later versions shipped a substantially rewritten 'Lightning Attention' that is NOT this algorithm, so citing these as the same thing would be wrong.
